The panel-reviewed SIU report field schema

Source: R/parse_siu.R
siusch.Rd

Returns the sixteen fields that the package extracts from every Ontario Special Investigations Unit (SIU) director's report, with a one-line description of each. Use it to see what siuprs() returns, to build an empty coding sheet for hand review, or to check which fields are counts before summing them across reports.

Usage

siusch()

Value

A data.frame with 16 rows and three columns: name (character, the field name used by siuprs()), count (logical, TRUE for the five count fields) and description (character, what the field records).

Details

The schema is held in the native core (src/siu_schema.h) and is the same list that siuprs() fills. Three fields are dates in ISO YYYY-MM-DD form, five are counts and the rest are free text. Count-type fields (count = TRUE) count distinct entities, and zero is a real answer: a witness-official-only investigation has zero subject officials. The function takes no arguments, reads no files and uses no network.

Examples

s <- siusch()
s$name
#>  [1] "police_service"                "date_of_incident_iso"         
#>  [3] "date_siu_notified_iso"         "date_of_director_decision_iso"
#>  [5] "siu_investigators"             "siu_forensics_investigators"  
#>  [7] "number_of_witness_officials"   "number_of_civilian_witnesses" 
#>  [9] "number_of_subject_officials"   "age_affected"                 
#> [11] "sex_gender_affected"           "charges_recommended"          
#> [13] "directors_name"                "location_of_call"             
#> [15] "specific_injuries"             "relevant_legislation"         

# only the count fields
s[s$count, c("name", "description")]
#>                           name
#> 5            siu_investigators
#> 6  siu_forensics_investigators
#> 7  number_of_witness_officials
#> 8 number_of_civilian_witnesses
#> 9  number_of_subject_officials
#>                                                                                        description
#> 5                                                         the number of SIU investigators assigned
#> 6                                                the number of SIU forensic investigators assigned
#> 7                                            the count of distinct WITNESS officers/officials (WO)
#> 8                                                    the count of distinct civilian witnesses (CW)
#> 9 the count of distinct SUBJECT officers/officials (SO); a witness-officer-only investigation is 0

# an empty hand-coding sheet with one column per field
sheet <- as.data.frame(setNames(replicate(nrow(s), character(0), simplify = FALSE),
                                 s$name))
ncol(sheet)
#> [1] 16
